subject: Usage thermostat check & expansion recommendation
messages:
From: Kelly O'Neill <kelly@thermadata.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@thermadata.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly consumption check ahead of renewal

Hi Naomi,

Heads up — our renewal is coming up in September and we saw a ~38% spike in token consumption over the past 6 weeks compared to Q2 baseline. Latency for some Gen-2 workflows has crept up (intermittent 150–220ms tail). Procurement wants a concise health/ROI snapshot so they can decide on commit uplift vs. burst credits.

Can you share: 1) an itemized usage breakdown (models + endpoints + tokens), 2) a short ROI/efficiency note (we’re especially interested in cost per 1M tokens after discounts), and 3) any recommended scaling options (commit vs. burst vs. quantization change) with risks?

I’m looping Procurement — they prefer a single-slide summary plus the raw CSV.

Thanks,
Kelly
Kelly O'Neill
Head of ML Ops — ThermaData
kelly@thermadata.com

Attachment: request-specs.txt (1KB text stub)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Kelly O'Neill <kelly@thermadata.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly consumption check ahead of renewal

Thanks for the note, Kelly — we’ll get you a concise packet. Quick readout and proposed next steps below; full export + report to follow by Monday.

Snapshot (high level):
- Recent spike: +38% YoY token use (approx. 2.1B tokens in last 30d) concentrated on the "session-scoring" endpoint (model: rdx-3b-v2) and a smaller uplift on embeddings.
- Tail latency: median is stable (~60–90ms); 95th percentile moved from 120ms -> 190–220ms during peak windows (sustained 10–15 minute bursts).
- Cost pressure: current effective cost (net) is ~$12.8 per 1M tokens (after existing volume tier).

Initial recommendations:
1) Move to a modest commitment uplift: +20% committed tokens for 6 months to secure better unit pricing (projected 12% effective cost reduction).
2) Add a 1M-token burst credit pool for seasonal spikes (keeps infra resilient during the 10–15 minute storms).
3) Short canary: route 10% of session-scoring traffic to rdx-3b-q (quantized variant) to measure latency and cost delta before a full roll.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync with Procurement and Ben (SE) early next week to walk the packet? I’ll attach the CSV, latency PDF, and a proposed amendment draft.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly consumption check ahead of renewal (analysis)

Naomi / Grace — I ran the token-by-endpoint drill and produced the CSV. Key numbers to call out for the sync:
- Session-scoring (rdx-3b-v2): 1.45B tokens (69% of spend), avg prompt len 220 tokens, avg response len 60 tokens.
- Embeddings: 420M tokens (20% of spend), mostly for nightly batch jobs.
- Other endpoints (chat/rerank): 230M tokens.

Cost sensitivity: a 20% commitment uplift reduces effective cost to ~$11.25 / 1M tokens (assuming current tier multipliers). If we combine that with a 10% routing to the q-variant we estimate a further ~$0.9 / 1M improvement after measuring quality delta.

Latency note: the 95th percentile spikes correspond with an autoscaling lag when concurrent prefix caching misses hit (~2–3 seconds of provisioning). The short-term mitigation is a small headroom reservation during business hours (we can configure this in Dedicated or via a headroom policy for Hosted).

I attached the raw CSV slice and a sample SQL used to generate the pivot (included as a small text stub in the CSV).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@thermadata.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly consumption check ahead of renewal

Hi Kelly / team — attached are the files Ben produced plus a short two-page summary (see attachments). Below is the single-slide executive summary for Procurement:

Executive summary:
- Observed behavior: 38% short-term consumption spike concentrated in session scoring (rdx-3b-v2). Performance: median latency fine; 95p increased to ~200ms in bursts.
- Economics: Current blended rate: $12.8 / 1M tokens. Option A (20% commit uplift, 6 months) -> projected blended $11.25 / 1M tokens, ~12% savings. Option B (no uplift, 1M burst pool) -> higher unit cost but avoids commit risk. Option C (10% canary to rdx-3b-q + 20% uplift) -> blended ~$10.4 / 1M tokens after measurement and if quality delta acceptable.
- Risk/ops: Canary reduces risk of model regressions; headroom reservation or a small Dedicated pool reduces tail latency by removing the provision lag.
- Ask: Procurement to confirm tolerance for modest commit uplift (we can stage invoicing across a 6-month flex), and to approve the DocuSign amendment template so we can lock pricing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement reviews proposed-amendment-thermadata.docx and returns redlines (I’ve included a tracked copy).
2) We schedule a 30-min canary/runbook review w/ Ben to validate routing policies and monitoring alerts.
3) If agreed, Redwood will provision a 1M-token burst pool and apply a 12% pricing adjustment for the amended term.

Links and notes:
- Renewal dashboard: https://app.redwood.com/deals/TD-2026-45 (includes live token burn + headroom config)
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ND-thermadata-amendment (placeholder link; final will be generated after redlines)

I’m available Wed-Fri this week for the procurement sync; proposing Wed 8/19 10:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Naomi
